user.title: Choose your valve
user.description: Pick a valve Home Assistant can see, or type its Bluetooth address (for example `AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF`). Close the Mira app on every phone first: the valve accepts only one connection at a time.

data_description.address: Valves are discovered through any connectable Bluetooth adapter or proxy.

bluetooth_confirm.description: Set up {name}? You will pair with it next, so have the shower controller within reach.

pair_method.title: Pair with the valve
pair_method.description: The valve only talks over a bonded Bluetooth connection, and the bond lives on the adapter or proxy that connects to it. A bond made on a different adapter or phone does not count.

pair.title: Put the valve in pairing mode
pair.description:
1. Close the Mira app on every phone.
2. Press and hold the button on the front of the shower controller for about 5 seconds, until it flashes. On a dial model, use Menu, Settings, Connect.
3. Within 30 seconds, select **Submit**.

Home Assistant will bond with {address} and read its state. No water will run.

already_paired.title: Connect over the existing bond
already_paired.description: Home Assistant will connect to {address} and read its state. No water will run. If this fails, go back and pair instead.

error.invalid_address: That isn't a Bluetooth address. Use the form AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.
error.not_found: No connectable Bluetooth adapter or proxy can see the valve right now. Check that a proxy is in range and the valve has power.
error.pairing_failed: Pairing failed. Make sure the controller is flashing and the Mira app is closed, then try again. Some proxies cannot pair; see the README for pairing on the proxy itself.
error.cannot_connect: Connected, but the valve didn't answer. It usually means another device (often the Mira app) holds the connection, or the adapter has no bond with the valve.

abort.not_supported: This looks like an older Mira Mode valve, which uses a different protocol that this integration doesn't support.

init.title: Outlets
init.description: Name each outlet the way it is plumbed in your home (for example Shower, Bath or Handset). Leave a label empty to hide that outlet. The valve's own presets show which outlet feeds what.

not_found.message: No connectable Bluetooth adapter or proxy can see the valve.

not_following.message: The valve acknowledged the command but isn't running the outlets that were asked for.

start.name: Start
start.description: Runs an outlet at a temperature and flow. This runs real hot water.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Water temperature, 30-45 °C. Defaults to the Temperature setting.

flow.name: Flow
flow.description: Flow, 1-100 %. Defaults to the Flow setting.
